subject: biology

items.q: What is the correct order of organisation?
items.why: A tissue is a group of similar cells; organs are made of tissues; organ systems are groups of organs.

items.q: Can a single cell be a complete living organism?
items.correct: Yes — many organisms (e.g. amoeba, bacteria) are single-celled.
items.misconception: No, life always needs many cells.
items.random_wrong: Only plant cells can live alone.
items.why: Unicellular organisms carry out all life processes within one cell.

items.q: Do the body's organs work independently?
items.correct: No — they work together in organ systems.
items.misconception: Yes, each organ works completely on its own.
items.random_wrong: Only the brain affects other organs.
items.why: For example the heart, blood and vessels form the circulatory system, working together.

items.correct: A group of similar cells working together.
items.why: Tissues (e.g. muscle tissue) are groups of similar specialised cells; several tissues form an organ.
